subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: What enforceable Private/Secret/Incognito session contract should OpenClaw support before implementation begins?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent boundary affects privacy guarantees, storage, plugin APIs, channel commands/defaults, diagnostics, and user-facing UI promises, so automation should not choose the threat model or compatibility shape.

options.title: Design one cross-layer contract
options.body: Approve a single private/ephemeral session marker and enforcement model spanning protocol, store/transcripts, memory/compaction, plugins, channel triggers, and UI before any implementation PR lands.

options.title: Narrow to demo-only context suppression
options.body: Limit the first phase to an explicit UI mode that suppresses bootstrap context but does not claim no persistence, reducing scope while leaving the stronger privacy request open.

options.title: Defer until storage architecture is ready
options.body: Keep the issue open but do not sponsor implementation until session storage, plugin persistence, and artifact ownership can support a credible no-write guarantee.

recommendation.title: Design one cross-layer contract
recommendation.body: Approve a single private/ephemeral session marker and enforcement model spanning protocol, store/transcripts, memory/compaction, plugins, channel triggers, and UI before any implementation PR lands.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already carried the canonical review and is the strongest routing candidate for privacy/security product direction across session, memory, and runtime seams.
